overview: Serbia is a landlocked country in the Balkans. Its capital and largest city is Belgrade, which stands where the Sava river joins the Danube. Serbia was the largest republic of Yugoslavia. Kosovo, in the south, declared independence from Serbia in 2008, which Serbia does not recognise.

geography.text: Northern Serbia, a region called Vojvodina, is flat and fertile, part of the Pannonian Plain. Further south the land becomes hilly and then mountainous. The Danube flows through the country and cuts through the dramatic Iron Gates gorge on the border with Romania.

history.text: The medieval Serbian state reached its height under Emperor Stefan Dušan in the 1300s, before it was defeated by the Ottomans, most famously at the Battle of Kosovo in 1389. Serbia won self-rule and then full independence in 1878. It was the largest part of Yugoslavia from 1918, and after Yugoslavia broke up in wars in the 1990s, it became a separate state again in 2006.

events.title: Battle of Kosovo
events.text: A legendary battle against the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Serbia's independence is recognised at the Congress of Berlin.

events.title: Separate state
events.text: Serbia becomes fully separate after Montenegro votes for independence.

government.text: Serbia is a parliamentary republic. The National Assembly chooses the Prime Minister, while the President, elected directly every five years, has considerable influence. Serbia is a candidate to join the European Union. It does not recognise Kosovo, which declared independence in 2008.

economy.text: Serbia's economy includes car manufacturing, farming, food processing, mining and a growing IT sector in Belgrade and Novi Sad. Foreign companies from Europe and China have invested heavily in factories and mines.

culture.text: Serbian is written in both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets. Medieval Serbian Orthodox monasteries, such as Studenica, are famous for their wall paintings. The inventor Nikola Tesla, a pioneer of electricity, was an ethnic Serb, and Belgrade's airport and a museum are named after him.

items.title: Nikola Tesla
items.text: His work on alternating current helped power the modern world.

items.title: EXIT Festival
items.text: A huge music festival held in a fortress in Novi Sad.

items.title: Slava
items.text: A family's yearly feast for its patron saint, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Serbia is a powerhouse in team sports: basketball, water polo and volleyball. Novak Djokovic, from Belgrade, has won more Grand Slam men's singles titles than anyone else. The basketball star Nikola Jokić has won three NBA Most Valuable Player awards.

items.title: Novak Djokovic
items.text: 24 Grand Slam singles titles and Olympic gold in 2024.

didYouKnow: Serbia is one of the world's biggest exporters of raspberries.
The word 'vampire' entered English partly from Serbian folk tales.

keyPeople.text: Won a record 24 Grand Slam singles titles.
